title: Platform-level causal checks of the pair-bonding mechanisms in simulation
purpose: Measure whether the integrated bond state changes agent threat, help-seeking and partner affect in the predicted directions against simulated partners. These are simulation sanity and causal checks with common random numbers, not human results.

stable_husband_1999.source: Gottman, Swanson & Murray 1999 Table 1 stable husband: inertia .40, uninfluenced .72/24

ojive_mismatch.source: step influence with 1999 group-mean thresholds /24 and declared plateaus; outside the agent's bilinear model class

own_mood.description: express own mood valence; no steering

mirror.description: express the partner's last affect (unbounded accommodation)

declared_choices: Published 1999 parameters are on the -24..+24 SPAFF scale; they are divided by 24 to the agent's [-1,1] affect scale. Influence slopes are not published and are declared engineering values with negative influence stronger than positive, following the authors' recurring observation.
The simulated partner replies every turn; support after a request is a Bernoulli draw with the condition's responsiveness; the agent requests support exactly when its actuation context recommends it.
Common random numbers: the reference (bonding disabled) agent receives the identical task stream as the bonded agent for each seed.
In-memory SQLite and the snapshot storage backend are used for speed; storage backend does not change any numerical transition.

Attachment task stream: mild shocks with episodic setbacks (probability .12 per turn to start an episode of 3-6 turns of quality -.9, control .1, uncertainty .9); the partner speaks on half of the turns and always on the turn after a request. Episode parameters were chosen on a separate pilot seed so that arousal visits all three bands; they were not tuned to the endpoints.
Responsiveness updates once per resolved request at the published rate alpha_resp=.03, so the attachment experiment uses 240 turns; the dyad experiment uses 120 turns with a final window of 40.
